To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the properties of dense baryonic matter and compact stars are sensitive to the density dependence of the nuclear symmetry energy, that the onset of hyperons in neutron star cores leads to the softening of the equation of state and that the cooling of neutron stars is affected by the presence of superfluid phases and by neutrino radiation from the stellar interior.

the physics of dense matter is governed by the strong interaction and that the properties of dense baryonic phases and the cooling of compact stars are strongly affected by the neutrino radiation processes that are determined by the properties of dense matter.

(1) the symmetry energy and the onset of hyperons have a profound effect on the equation of state and the structure of compact stars; (2) the onset of superfluidity and superconductivity has a profound effect on neutrino emission rates from compact stars, and (3) the cooling of compact stars can be used to determine the symmetry energy, and the onset of the hyperon and meson condensates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the properties of dense matter at and above nuclear saturation density.
the study of dense baryonic matter within the Green’s function method and its applications to the physics of compact stars.
the physics of hadronic matter in compact stars and its observable consequences, in particular, neutrino cooling of neutron stars.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have no clear evidence for the existence of exotic phases of matter in neutron stars, but that the physics of dense matter and compact stars is still in an early stage of development.

the properties of hadrons and the equation of state of dense matter are still not known to a satisfactory degree of accuracy and that the present state of knowledge is insufficient for making definite statements on the composition and structure of neutron stars.

the physics of compact stars is a very promising field to study dense hadronic matter, and the physics of compact star cooling is a very promising tool to constrain the properties of hadron matter at and above nuclear matter saturation density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the physics of hadronic matter and neutrino radiation from neutron stars is well understood, and that the present observations do not contradict the standard picture.
the physics of dense hadrons and their interactions is still not well understood, and that more work is required to make progress in this area of research.

the properties of dense matter in neutron stars are not only important for our understanding of the equation of state of baryonic systems but also for the physics of neutrino radiation from compact stellar objects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a unified microscopic theory of dense baryonic matter is required to understand the properties of compact stars.

neutrino interactions with matter are a key element of the physics of compact stars and that the study of these processes is essential in order to understand the properties of hadron matter at high densities.
